sourceText: We’ve Been Trying to Reach You About Your Soul’s Extended Warranty  You’ve heard the phone call. Now imagine it taking a slightly different turn.  This short Christian comedy sketch borrows the familiar extended-warranty sales pitch to point toward a serious question: Are we simply calling Jesus Lord, or are we actually following Him?  In Matthew 7:21, Jesus warns that saying the right words isn’t the same as doing His Father’s will. It’s a passage worth opening our Bibles and reading carefully—including the verses that follow.  The telemarketing routine is a joke. Jesus’ warning deserves our attention.  Anchor Verse  “Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of My Father in heaven.” — Matthew 7:21, NKJV  Reflection Verses  Matthew 7:22–23 — Religious claims and impressive works don’t substitute for being known by Jesus.  Matthew 7:24–27 — Jesus compares hearing and doing His words to building a house on rock.  Luke 6:46 — Jesus asks why people call Him Lord while failing to do what He says.  Ephesians 2:8–10 — Salvation is God’s gift of grace through faith. Those created anew in Christ are called to walk in good works.  Additional Insights  The “warranty” and “compliance issue” language belongs to the parody. The underlying invitation is to examine ourselves honestly in light of Jesus’ teaching.  Matthew 7:21–23 challenges false assurance based on religious words and accomplishments. It isn’t saying that someone can purchase salvation through good behavior or that every stumble means God has rejected them.  Read the whole passage. Bring what you find before God, and ask Him to reveal where your actions need to catch up with your confession.  If this made you smile—and gave you something to think about—please consider liking, subscribing, or sharing.  #ChristianComedy #ChristianHumor #Matthew721 #FollowJesus #AVoiceCallingOut
